answer:
Things worth raising at your check-up:

1. Positive stool test with no follow-up on record. Your FIT on 2025-11-04 was positive. A positive FIT should be followed by a colonoscopy, and I find no colonoscopy, referral or note about it afterwards. This is the most important item and nearly a year old.

2. Diabetes check-ups and tests. Your A1c went from 6.5-6.6% in 2023 up to 8.3% in January 2025, then improved to 6.9% in February 2026. Metformin was stopped in April 2024 and you are now on Jardiance. There is no A1c since February 2026, so one is due. I also see no urine albumin test, eye exam or foot exam recorded, which are usually done yearly in diabetes.

3. Cholesterol. In February 2025 your LDL was 131 and total cholesterol 212 (both high). Atorvastatin 20 mg is listed from 2025-02-20, but there is no cholesterol test since, so we don't know whether it is working. Ask for a repeat lipid panel.

4. Vaccines. No immunizations are recorded at all. At 69 with diabetes, ask about flu, COVID, pneumococcal, shingles, RSV and Tdap. They may have been given elsewhere.

5. The July 2025 chest pain episode looks settled: the CT scan showed no pulmonary embolism and the chest wall pain resolved. The scan did note mild degenerative changes in the thoracic spine, which is only worth mentioning if you have back pain.

6. Other routine screening (mammogram, bone density) is not in these records, so I can't say whether it is up to date.

Your kidney function and potassium were normal in February 2026.
short: FIT positive 2025-11-04 with no colonoscopy on record; no A1c since 2026-02 (6.9%); LDL 131 in 2025-02 with no repeat after starting atorvastatin; no immunizations or diabetic eye/foot/urine albumin checks recorded.
